title: Understanding OCD: Symptoms, Treatment, and Daily Challenges - Obsessive Compulsive Disorder

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你们能通过出卖时间赚钱之外还能赚到钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动收入和经常性收入来源。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一个好消息要宣布。

sentences.en: Sophie Foote's One-to-Many programme is now open for enrolment.
sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特的“一对多”项目现已开放报名。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，例如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the programme myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我自己于2022年完成了这个项目，此后也一直支持两期心理学家走过他们的成长历程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的专属推广链接加入，你将获得苏菲的奖励以及我提供的独家支持礼包，无需额外付费。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalised guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 其中包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四次小组智囊团指导、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南&梅森礼品，以及限时一对一教练指导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrolment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10pm.
sentences.zh: 报名截止时间为11月16日星期一晚上10点。

sentences.en: Find out more via my bonus page linked in the description.
sentences.zh: 通过简介中链接的我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.en: And remember, you must purchase through my link to receive my bonuses.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.en: I'm here if you have any questions.
sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时在线。

sentences.en: Do you really know what OCD is?
sentences.zh: 你真的知道什么是强迫症（OCD）吗？

sentences.en: Spoiler alert, it is not just about being neat and tidy.
sentences.zh: 剧透预警，它不仅仅是保持干净整洁那么简单。

sentences.en: In this episode, we uncover the truth about OCD, the distress it causes and the treatments that can help.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将揭开强迫症的真相、它所带来的痛苦以及可以提供帮助的治疗方法。

sentences.en: If you or someone you care about struggles with intrusive thoughts and compulsive behaviours, this is one you're not going to want to miss.
sentences.zh: 如果你或你关心的人正在与侵入性思维和强迫行为作斗争，这绝对是你不想错过的一期节目。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎收听。

sentences.en: I am Dr. Marianne and I'm a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安博士，我是一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: Now, OCD does get spoken about by lots and lots of people, but often in quite a throwaway manner.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多人都在谈论强迫症，但往往是以一种相当随意的态度。

sentences.en: This is not that.
sentences.zh: 这可不是那种节目。

sentences.en: I spend a great deal of my time as a clinical psychologist and providing therapy for people who are really, you know,
sentences.zh: 我作为临床心理学家花了很多时间，为那些真正……你知道的,

sentences.en: have their lives very much affected by the far-reaching implications of OCD.
sentences.zh: 生活深受强迫症深远影响的人提供治疗。

sentences.en: So this episode is all about what it is, how it can take hold.
sentences.zh: 所以本期节目主要探讨它是什么，以及它是如何占据主导地位的。

sentences.en: And, you know, we're trying to normalise and validate people's experiences so that they are more able to grapple with this and to be able to take control.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我们试图将人们的经历正常化和正当化，以便他们能够更好地应对并掌控自己的人生。

sentences.en: If you find this helpful, wherever you are watching or listening, please do like, subscribe, drop some comments and give this video some love.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这有帮助，无论你在哪里观看或收听，请点赞、订阅、留言并给这个视频一点支持。

sentences.en: I will look forward to catching up with you on the other side and I hope you find it really, really useful.
sentences.zh: 我期待在节目的另一端与你交流，希望你觉得它真的、真的很实用。

sentences.en: Hi, I just want to welcome along our guest for today, Faye.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我只想欢迎我们今天的嘉宾费伊。

sentences.en: Hi, welcome along to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗨，欢迎来到本播客。

sentences.en: Hi, thanks, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 嗨，谢谢你，玛丽安。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: Thank you for pitching your idea for the episode to us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你向我们提出本期节目的选题构想。

sentences.en: Before we crack on with our content, thinking about OCD and striving for careers, could you tell the audience and myself a little bit about you, please, Faye?
sentences.zh: 在我们深入探讨关于强迫症和职业追求的内容之前，费伊，你能向我和听众简单介绍一下你自己吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so my name's Faye.
sentences.zh: 好的，我叫费伊。

sentences.en: I am a psychological well-being practitioner or PWP for short, very recently qualified.
sentences.zh: 我是一名心理健康从业人员，简称PWP，最近刚刚获得资格认证。

sentences.en: So just to give a brief overview, I work with people with common mental health difficulties, depression, anxiety, OCD, you know, those sorts of things.
sentences.zh: 简单概述一下，我与患有常见心理健康问题的人合作，比如抑郁症、焦虑症、强迫症，你知道的，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, and that's what I do as a full-time job.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我的全职工作。

sentences.en: I've worked in mental health for a few years now in various different roles before I got into doing the PWP work.
sentences.zh: 在从事PWP工作之前，我在心理健康领域工作了几年，担任过各种不同的角色。

sentences.en: And I am someone who also lives with OCD.
sentences.zh: 同时，我也是一名强迫症患者。

sentences.en: So that's a very important part of, you know, my role and me as a person as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是我的角色以及作为个人的我的非常重要的一部分。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: If people did want to hear more about what PWPs are and, you know, how they can train as one and what the reality of working as a PWP is like,
sentences.zh: 如果人们想更多地了解PWP是什么，以及，你知道的，他们如何接受培训成为一名PWP，以及作为PWP工作的现实情况是怎样的，

sentences.en: they can listen to the episode I recorded that was out very recently, actually, with Ben Olufsen.
sentences.zh: 他们可以收听我最近与本·奥尔夫森录制并发布的节目。

sentences.en: But let's hear a little bit more about you and OCD.
sentences.zh: 但让我们来多了解一下你和你的强迫症。

sentences.en: So when did that first become apparent?
sentences.zh: 那么，这最早是什么时候显现出来的？

sentences.en: Maybe not to yourself, maybe to other people.
sentences.zh: 也许对你自己不明显，但对其他人而言呢？

sentences.en: When was that first in your life?
sentences.zh: 它第一次出现在你的生命中是什么时候？

sentences.en: So it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这挺有趣的。

sentences.en: I think with OCD, obviously, what we often think of it is, it can be really apparent to the people around you.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于强迫症，显而易见的是，我们通常认为它对周围的人来说会非常明显。

sentences.en: But my OCD tended to manifest in more sort of mental compulsions rather than physical.
sentences.zh: 但我的强迫症往往表现为更多的精神强迫，而不是身体上的。

sentences.en: So it wasn't always obvious to the people who were around me.
sentences.zh: 所以它对我身边的人来说并不总是那么显眼。

sentences.en: I think probably, you know, looking back, it started maybe when I was around 17, 18 years old, but I didn't get sort of diagnosed until later on, until I was, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想可能，你知道的，回想起来，它可能始于我17、18岁左右，但我直到后来才被确诊，直到我……你知道的，

sentences.en: around sort of 21, 22.
sentences.zh: 大概21、22岁左右。

sentences.en: So it was a bit of a journey to kind of, you know, come to terms with that, you know, what was going on.
sentences.zh: 所以，要接受并弄清楚到底发生了什么，经历了一段曲折的过程。

sentences.en: I didn't know a lot about OCD at the time that I started experiencing it.
sentences.zh: 在我刚开始经历强迫症时，我对它知之甚少。

sentences.en: So for me, it was very difficult to kind of have that inward battle and feel like you're the only person in the world who's experiencing this.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，进行那种内心的斗争并感觉自己是世界上唯一一个经历这一切的人是非常困难的。

sentences.en: Just not knowing what was going on was really scary.
sentences.zh: 仅仅不知道发生了什么就真的很可怕。

sentences.en: So when I sort of started to think that maybe this might be OCD,
sentences.zh: 所以当我开始认为这可能是强迫症时，

sentences.en: I remember sort of Googling a lot of my symptoms at the time and it would come up with all these different OCD foruMs.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时在谷歌上搜索了很多我的症状，结果会跳出所有这些不同的强迫症论坛。

sentences.en: And I thought, well, that can't be me because I don't, you know, excessively wash my hands.
sentences.zh: 我想，这不可能是我的情况，因为我没有，你知道的，过度洗手。

sentences.en: I'm not like very particular about where I put things, though I brushed it off for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 我对东西放在哪里也不是特别讲究，所以我很长一段时间都没放在心上。

sentences.en: And, you know, the more I sort of got into that Googling spiral, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我越是陷入那个谷歌搜索的漩涡中，

sentences.en: as people with OCD often tend to do, it was becoming a bit more apparent to me that actually, you know,
sentences.zh: 正如患有强迫症的人经常做的那样，我越来越清楚地意识到，其实，你知道的，

sentences.en: maybe OCD is something a bit more than just sort of, you know, cleanliness and orderliness.
sentences.zh: 也许强迫症不仅仅是清洁和整洁那么简单。

sentences.en: So, yeah, that's when I kind of started to notice.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这就是我开始注意到的时候。

sentences.en: Yeah, you make such a brilliant point there that it's not just about, you know, switching on and off light switches or, you know, getting the gas dials on your hob just right.
sentences.zh: 是的，你提出了一个绝妙的观点，它不仅关乎，你知道的，开关电灯开关，或者，你知道的，把炉灶上的煤气旋钮调得正合适。

sentences.en: You know, what OCD is and how I explain it to clients that I work with.
sentences.zh: 你知道，什么是强迫症以及我是如何向我的客户解释的。

sentences.en: I should also say that you and I have never worked together therapeutically.
sentences.zh: 我还应该说明，你和我从未在治疗上合作过。

sentences.en: This is a professional chat, so I hope that this feels okay, but please let me know if it doesn't and we can cut any bits out that don't work for you.
sentences.zh: 这是一次专业的聊天，所以我希望这感觉还好，如果不好的话请告诉我，我们可以删掉任何不适合你的部分。

sentences.en: As I explain OCD to everybody, really, whether it's my clients or just people I chat with, OCD is, you know, an impulsive and intrusive thought that all of us might have.
sentences.zh: 正如我向所有人解释强迫症一样，无论是我的客户还是只是聊天的人，强迫症，你知道的，是我们所有人可能都会有的冲动和侵入性想法。

sentences.en: It might be a really logical thought about something that becomes distressing and it's then the activity that you take to kind of neutralize and to bring that distress down with a belief that that will somehow help that to not happen or that it will make the likelihood of something else happen.
sentences.zh: 它可能是一个关于某事的非常符合逻辑的想法，但却变得令人痛苦，然后你采取行动去中和并降低这种痛苦，坚信这会以某种方式阻止事情发生，或者降低其他事情发生的可能性。

sentences.en: So, for example, somebody has a thought that, oh, it's cold out there, it's dark, and then they think, you know, it's a sense they make of that.
sentences.zh: 例如，有人有个想法，哦，外面好冷，天好黑，然后他们想，你知道的，这是他们对这件事的解读。

sentences.en: Oh, you know, my loved one is actually still out at the moment.
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道，我爱的人现在其实还在外面。

sentences.en: Then they begin to make, you know, their attributions to that.
sentences.zh: 然后他们开始，你知道的，把他们的归因强加于此。

sentences.en: You know, I'm worried that something might happen to them because it is so cold and so dark.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我担心他们可能会发生什么，因为天气又冷又黑。

sentences.en: Like, gosh, that would be awful, that would be horrendous, or maybe I'll, you know, I'll have to sit and do this all, you know, 15 times until it feels right.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那太可怕了，那太骇人了，或者也许我，你知道的，我得坐下来把这事做上15遍，直到感觉对了为止。

sentences.en: And I'm sorry for anyone listening to that on MP3.
sentences.zh: 对于通过MP3收听的人，我感到很抱歉。

sentences.en: I was clicking a pen there, if you're not watching it on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是在YouTube上观看的话，我刚才在按一支笔。

sentences.en: I was clicking, you know, a multicolour pen, but it's that sense of until it feels right or until it feels manageable.
sentences.zh: 我按了一支，你知道的，多色笔，但那种感觉就是直到感觉对了，或者直到感觉可以控制了。

sentences.en: And that might be different on different days.
sentences.zh: 而且在不同的日子里，这可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: And what we know is that that can change.
sentences.zh: 我们知道的是，情况是会改变的。

sentences.en: So what initially kind of placates that and brings the distress down doesn't always work.
sentences.zh: 所以最初能平息这种焦虑并减轻痛苦的方法并不总是管用。

sentences.en: Or the one strategy stops working over time.
sentences.zh: 或者某种策略随着时间的推移停止起作用。

sentences.en: And then you kind of have to ramp it up.
sentences.zh: 然后你不得不加大力度。

sentences.en: And that's when it really begins to impact on your well-being.
sentences.zh: 这就是它真正开始对你的幸福感产生影响的时候。

sentences.en: And sometimes your functioning and your ability to look after yourself and strive for normal basic functions, let alone a career.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至会影响你的机能以及照顾自己和争取实现基本正常生活的能力，更不用说追求职业生涯了。

sentences.en: Does that encapsulate your experience of OCD?
sentences.zh: 这概括了你对强迫症的体验吗？

sentences.en: Do you understand it feel different?
sentences.zh: 你理解它还是觉得有何不同？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, I completely agree with what you've said there.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，我完全同意你刚才所说的话。

sentences.en: And, you know, the main thing is, and I think as explained quite nicely there, it's the compulsion that is the part that can really begin to take over your life.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，最重要的一点，而且正如刚才解释得很好的那样，强迫症真正开始接管你生活的正是强迫行为本身。

sentences.en: You know, it's not the thoughts themselves, although they are really distressing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，并不是想法本身，尽管它们确实非常痛苦。

sentences.en: The compulsions are really what sort of has a big impact on sort of well-being, functioning.
sentences.zh: 强迫行为才是真正对幸福感和机能产生重大影响的因素。

sentences.en: If you have a compulsion that you need to do over and over and over again, and you can't, you know, move on to something until that compulsion feels right,
sentences.zh: 如果你有一种强迫行为，你需要一遍又一遍地做，而且你不能，你知道的，在强迫行为感觉对之前转移到其他事情上去，

sentences.en: or it feels that you've done it enough times, or, you know, that anxiety has eventually lowered.
sentences.zh: 或者感觉你已经做得够多了，或者，你知道的，焦虑最终消退了。

sentences.en: It impacts on everything, you know, it impacts on your ability to work.
sentences.zh: 它会影响一切，你知道的，它会影响你的工作能力。

sentences.en: It can impact on your ability to, you know, there were times and, you know,
sentences.zh: 它会影响你的能力，你知道的，曾经有一段时间，而且，你知道的，

sentences.en: lengthy periods of time where I struggled to get out of bed because I was going through these mental compulsions in my head.
sentences.zh: 有很长一段时间我很难起床，因为我在脑海里经历着这些精神强迫。

sentences.en: And it took me so long that by the time the anxiety had lowered, you know, it could have been minutes, hours later.
sentences.zh: 这花了我很长时间，以至于当焦虑消退时，你知道的，可能已经是几分钟或几小时后了。

sentences.en: And the thing is that, you know, that anxiety does eventually lower, but oftentimes what happens then is, you know, you've done that compulsion, you feel better.
sentences.zh: 问题是，你知道的，焦虑最终确实会消退，但通常接下来发生的是，你知道的，你做完了那个强迫行为，你感觉好些了。

sentences.en: And a few minutes later, there's a new intrusive thought and you have to go through the whole process again.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，又出现了一个新的侵入性想法，你不得不经历整个过程。

sentences.en: So, it can be extremely time consuming.
sentences.zh: 所以，这可能非常耗时。

sentences.en: And I think that is when sometimes it can start to become apparent to the other people around you as well that something's not quite right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么有时它开始变得对你周围的其他其他人也显而易见，即有些事情不太对劲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Distress is the word that probably isn't always spoken about enough with OCD.
sentences.zh: 痛苦这个词可能在谈论强迫症时往往没有被足够多地提及。

sentences.en: This is deeply distressing.
sentences.zh: 这是极其痛苦的。

sentences.en: And, you know, it's not a case of as often people will try and help you.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，这不像人们经常试图对你提供帮助时那样。

sentences.en: Come on, just stop it.
sentences.zh: 拜托，停下来就行了。

sentences.en: Just stop it.
sentences.zh: 停下来就行了。

sentences.en: It's not that easy.
sentences.zh: 没那么简单。

sentences.en: This is deeply distressing.
sentences.zh: 这是极其痛苦的。

sentences.en: And, you know, often it will crop up.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，它经常会突然出现。

sentences.en: You know, I heard you say that it was around 17.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我听到你说那大约是在17岁的时候。

sentences.en: And I know that's a really key time for mocks, for AS levels, for A levels, perhaps for kind of college stuff.
sentences.zh: 我知道那是模拟考试、AS水准考试、A水准考试以及大学预科的关键时期。

sentences.en: But also, you know, people's health might falter, parents' health might falter.
sentences.zh: 但同时，你知道的，人们的健康可能会恶化，父母的健康可能会恶化。

sentences.en: And then it puts that stresses, those cracks on or maybe the anxiety of having to kind of be independent, get around to college.
sentences.zh: 然后它带来了压力，带来了裂痕，或者也许是不得不独立的焦虑，四处去上大学。

sentences.en: There can be so many things at whatever time of life it is that kind of, yeah, leave that vulnerability for OCD to be able to get in.
sentences.zh: 无论在人生的哪个阶段，都可能有很多事情，是的，会留下让强迫症趁虚而入的脆弱性。

sentences.en: And even when in recovery and in remission or in between chunks of OCD,
sentences.zh: 甚至在康复、缓解期间，或者在强迫症发作的间隙，

sentences.en: it's really important to kind of look after well-being and self-care to try and safeguard from finding its way in again as a strategy.
sentences.zh: 照顾好自己的身心健康和自我关怀真的非常重要，以此来防范它再次作为一种策略潜入进来。

sentences.en: Because it's like, you know, if we're thinking of externalizing it, it's like it almost whiskers to you, you know.
sentences.zh: 因为这就像是，你知道的，如果我们试着将它拟人化，它几乎是在对你耳语，你知道的。

sentences.en: It's just going to be, this is going to make it bad.
sentences.zh: 它只会是，这会让事情变糟。

sentences.en: This is going to make you feel better.
sentences.zh: 这会让你感觉好些。

sentences.zh: 我认为关于强迫行为需要了解的重要一点是，它们可能非常不同，并且因人而异。

sentences.en: I know a big one for me was kind of this feeling of having to sort of tell people, you know, sort of confession.
sentences.zh: 我知道对我很重要的一点是这种不得不告诉别人、你知道的、有点像忏悔的感觉。

sentences.en: So I had a period where I was very focused on sort of being kind of morally correct and, and everything being perfect and never telling any kind of lies or anything like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我有一段时间非常专注于保持道德上的正确，以及一切都完美无缺，绝不撒谎或做类似的事情。

sentences.en: So it could be something as, you know, inconsequential as I told someone, oh, this person was wearing a pink shirt.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能是不那么重要的事，比如我告诉某人，哦，这个人穿了一件粉红色的衬衫。

sentences.en: And then a few minutes later, I realized, oh, actually, that person was actually wearing a blue shirt and that would take up, you know,

sentences.zh: 这会给我带来巨大的痛苦，因为我没有完全说实话。

sentences.en: That I would have to go back and correct myself and say to this person, oh, actually, I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 以至于我不得不回去纠正自己，对这个人说，哦，实际上，我弄错了。

sentences.en: That person was actually wearing a blue shirt, not a pink shirt.
sentences.zh: 那个人其实穿的是一件蓝色衬衫，而不是粉色衬衫。

sentences.en: And that would be what I would have to do to kind of, you know, I suppose, bring that anxiety down and make me feel better.
sentences.zh: 为了，你知道的，我想，把焦虑降下来，让自己感觉好点，我不得不这样做。

sentences.en: So, you know, that is a huge part of it.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是其中很大一部分。

sentences.en: Also, you know, maybe asking for reassurance around things, counting sort of inside your head is a huge mental compulsion for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 还有，你知道的，可能会要求得到关于某些事情的保证，在脑海里数数对许多人来说也是一个巨大的精神强迫。

sentences.en: Sort of going over things, mentally reviewing and, you know, there's a huge subset, I suppose, of OCD around maybe false memories.
sentences.zh: 反复琢磨事情，在脑海中回顾，并且，你知道的，关于强迫症有一个很大的子集，我想，可能是关于虚假记忆的。

sentences.en: So kind of thinking, having an intrusive thought and believing that thought has actually happened in the past or, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以有点像思考，产生一个侵入性想法，并坚信这个想法在过去实际发生过，或者，你知道的，

sentences.en: you've done something wrong or you've done something bad.
sentences.zh: 你做错了某事，或者你干了什么坏事。

sentences.en: And having to mentally sort of go back to that, you know, moment in time and review it and think, you know, what have I done here?
sentences.zh: 然后你必须在脑海里回溯到那个特定的时间点，去复盘、去想：我到底做了什么？

sentences.en: Did I do everything correctly?
sentences.zh: 我每件事都做对了吗？

sentences.en: Have I done something wrong?
sentences.zh: 我是不是做错了什么？

sentences.en: And just going over that event over and over again.
sentences.zh: 然后就是一遍又一遍地回想那个场景。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of different mental compulsions and they're not always visible to others or very apparent to others.
sentences.zh: 所以有很多不同的心理强迫行为，它们并不总是能被别人看到，或者对别人来说很明显。

sentences.en: That is a lot, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这压力真的很大，对吧？

sentences.en: It must really impact on every aspect of your life, your physical health, your mental health, your ability to do anything.

sentences.zh: 这真是一个极具分量的问题。

sentences.zh: 我想我内心深处一直都想从事心理健康方面的工作。

sentences.zh: 这是我非常热爱并且极其在乎的事情。

sentences.en: So I think that always helps.

sentences.en: But at that time, I was actually finishing off my undergraduate degree.

sentences.en: It was incredibly, incredibly difficult.

sentences.en: I won't sugarcoat it.
sentences.zh: 我绝不粉饰太平。

sentences.en: I would find myself incredibly pressed for time.

sentences.zh: 事实上，曾有一段时间我挂了很多科，因为我根本起不了床。

sentences.en: I could not get to the point of, you know, studying or even going to my lectures.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法集中精力去学习，或者去上课。

sentences.zh: 为此我错过了很多讲座。

sentences.en: And I eventually actually, you know, reset one of the exams that I failed.
sentences.zh: 后来我确实重考了一门挂掉的科目。

sentences.zh: 但因为我第二次又挂了，我被学校开除了。

sentences.en: But this was sort of after my second year.

sentences.en: So it was incredibly difficult.
sentences.zh: 所以那段经历极其艰难。

sentences.zh: 我确实会回想起那些日子，真遗憾我把时间都耗在室内、家里，根本起不了床，

sentences.en: because I was all consumed by OCD.

sentences.zh: 我想对我来说最难受的部分就是那种未知，

sentences.en: And, you know, there was something really, really wrong with me because I couldn't do the things that other people were doing.

sentences.zh: 还是说，你知道的，我要这样生活下去？

sentences.en: And with it becoming worse and worse, you know, with every passing day, because as you'd mentioned earlier on, it comes to a point where we kind of habituate
sentences.zh: 而且随着情况一天比一天变得更糟，你知道的，正如你刚才所提到的，我们会对那些强迫行为产生一种习惯化（habituate），

sentences.en: to those compulsions almost and we have to do more and more to make ourselves feel better.
sentences.zh: 几乎到了我们需要做越来越多的事情来让自己感觉好受一些的地步。

sentences.en: So the OCD only gets worse.
sentences.zh: 所以强迫症只会越来越严重。

sentences.en: Do I continue with that?
sentences.zh: 我是要继续那样下去吗？

sentences.en: Or do I, you know, commit to this therapy and, you know, this moment of the stress knowing that actually this is going to be really useful for me?
sentences.zh: 还是我，你知道的，要致力于这项疗法，并且经历这一刻的痛苦，深知这其实对我会非常有用？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: And reaching out to ask for help can feel like a really brave step, but it's really, really important.
sentences.zh: 伸出援手寻求帮助可能会让人觉得是非常勇敢的一步，但它真的、真的很重要。

sentences.en: And people do get better from OCD.
sentences.zh: 而且人们的强迫症确实会好起来。

sentences.en: You know, it might be that you use those strategies every day, but people get better and do have that meaningful, enjoyable life.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，可能你每天都在使用这些策略，但人们确实会好起来，并过上那种有意义、快乐的生活。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for sharing your wise insights with our audience.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你与我们的观众分享你充满智慧的见解。

sentences.en: Is there anything I haven't asked you that you think is important that we do cover or that we think about?
sentences.zh: 有什么问题是我没有问你，而你觉得我们必须涵盖或思考的重要事情吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think a huge thing that is really important and something that I didn't know sort of a few years back was that OCD is treated, you know, really widely throughout the NHS.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得有一件非常重要、而我几年前并不了解的大事，那就是强迫症在整个NHS（英国国民保健署）得到了非常广泛的治疗。

sentences.en: You know, I remember going through a phase where, you know, I thought that this was really uncommon disorder and it was going to be really difficult to get help.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我记得我曾经历过这样一个阶段，你知道的，我以为这是一种非常罕见的疾病，很难获得帮助。

sentences.en: But actually, you know, the talk and therapy services, you know, throughout the NHS across the UK, they all will bring you in and treat you for OCD and the practitioners there,
sentences.zh: 但实际上，你知道的，整个英国NHS的心理治疗服务（talking therapy services），他们都会接待你并治疗你的强迫症，那里的从业人员，

sentences.en: they do have an understanding of OCD.
sentences.zh: 他们确实对强迫症有着深刻的理解。

sentences.en: So I know it's really incredibly scary and incredibly difficult to reach out for that support and you don't always want to tell someone what's going on in your own head.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道寻求这种支持真的极其可怕、极其艰难，你并不总是想把脑子里发生的事告诉别人。

sentences.en: But just please be aware that, you know, there are trained professionals out there who know what you're going through, who will understand, who will listen to you
sentences.zh: 但请务必知道，你知道的，外面有受过专业培训的专业人士，他们知道你正在经历什么，他们会理解，会倾听你，

sentences.en: and will give you the help that you need.
sentences.zh: 并会给你提供你需要的帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 对，完全如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, just don't feel like you're struggling alone because, you know, people are just trying to make the best of worlds with these wild, tricky brains
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，不要觉得你是在孤军奋战，因为，你知道的，人们只是在试图用我们拥有的这些疯狂、狡猾的大脑，在世界上过得最好，

sentences.en: that we've got, you know, we're just humans and, you know, that's just how it is.
sentences.zh: 我们只是普通人，你知道的，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Wishing you well with your work as a PWP and beyond whatever that looks like for you and keep up with that mindfulness.
sentences.zh: 祝你作为PWP（心理 wellbeing 从业者）的工作以及未来无论对你意味着什么的任何方面一切顺利，并请继续保持正念。

sentences.en: Keep doing that.
sentences.zh: 继续这样做。

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: I will.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: Thanks, Marianne.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，玛丽安（Marianne）。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: You too.
sentences.zh: 你也是。

sentences.en: Thank you so much to our guest, Faye.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢我们的嘉宾费伊（Faye）。

sentences.en: I did forget to mention where you can catch up with Faye if you want to connect with her.
sentences.zh: 我确实忘了提如果你想联系费伊，可以在哪里找到她。

sentences.en: She is on LinkedIn and she is Faye with an E, so F-A-Y-E Wilson.
sentences.zh: 她在领英（LinkedIn）上，她的名字费伊拼写中有一个E，所以是 F-A-Y-E Wilson。

sentences.en: More about her and what she does.
sentences.zh: 更多关于她以及她所做的事情。

sentences.en: You can only follow her journey in her career too.
sentences.zh: 你也可以关注她职业生涯的旅程。

sentences.en: Please, if you are struggling with OCD or you care about somebody who is, please do book yourself a GP appointment or, you know, encourage someone that you love to do that.
sentences.zh: 拜托，如果你正在与强迫症挣扎，或者你在乎的人正在经历痛苦，请务必预约全科医生（GP），或者，你知道的，鼓励你爱的人去那样做。

sentences.en: Maybe offer to go with them if that would be useful.
sentences.zh: 如果觉得有帮助的话，或许可以主动提出和他们一起去。

sentences.en: You can also come and connect with me on my social media channels where I am,
sentences.zh: 你也可以来我的社交媒体渠道与我互动，我在那里是，

sentences.en: Dr. Marianne Trent, absolutely everywhere.
sentences.zh: Dr. Marianne Trent（玛丽安·特伦特博士），到处都是。

sentences.en: And I've got a sprinkling of different content that goes in different places as well.
sentences.zh: 我在不同地方也发布各种各样不同的内容。

sentences.en: So do come and follow me everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以一定要到处去关注我。

sentences.en: And of course, we've got the free
sentences.zh: 当然，我们还有免费的

sentences.en: Aspiring Psychologist Community Facebook group where you can come and watch the exclusive videos called Marianne's Motivation and Mindset, which happen weekly on Fridays.
sentences.zh: “有抱负的心理学家社区”Facebook群组，你可以在那里观看每周五定期播出的独家视频，名为“玛丽安的动力与心态”（Marianne's Motivation and Mindset）。

sentences.en: If it's your time and you're in the psychology profession, you're ready for the next step.
sentences.zh: 如果时机成熟，你身处心理学行业，并且准备好迈出下一步。

sentences.en: Please do also check out the Aspiring Psychologist membership.
sentences.zh: 请务必也查看“有抱负的心理学家会员计划”（Aspiring Psychologist membership）。

sentences.en: And if you found this video helpful, I know that you'll really find the one I did with Alexandra on OCD and complex trauma to be really useful as well.
sentences.zh: 如果你觉得这个视频有帮助，我知道你也会觉得我和亚历山大（Alexandra）关于强迫症和复杂性创伤的那个视频真的非常有用。

sentences.en: I will link that in the show notes and it will be on screen at the end of this for you to just click through and watch as well.
sentences.zh: 我会把它链接在节目说明中，在视频结束时也会出现在屏幕上，供你直接点击观看。

sentences.en: Please also consider the Aspiring Psychologist Collective book, the Clinical Psychologist Collective book, and the brand new kid on the block,
sentences.zh: 请同时考虑《有抱负的心理学家集体》一书、《临床心理学家集体》一书，以及最新推出的重磅新作，

sentences.en: An Autistic Anthology, which is real life stories of people with autism diagnosis talking about their experiences working in mental health.
sentences.zh: 《自闭症选集》（An Autistic Anthology），里面讲述了被诊断为自闭症的人在心理健康领域工作经历的真实生活故事。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being part of my world.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你成为我世界的一部分。

sentences.en: Do be kind to yourself.
sentences.zh: 请对自己好一点。

sentences.en: If you're looking to become a psychologist,
sentences.zh: 如果你想成为一名心理学家，

sentences.en: then let this be your guide.
sentences.zh: 那就让这成为你的指南。

sentences.en: With this podcast, that's your side.
sentences.zh: 有了这个播客，它就在你身旁。

sentences.en: You'll be on your way.
sentences.zh: 你将走上正轨。

sentences.en: It's the Aspiring Psychologist podcast with Dr. Marianne Trent.
sentences.zh: 这是由玛丽安·特伦特博士主持的《有抱负的心理学家播客》（The Aspiring Psychologist podcast）。

sentences.en: Psychologists, what if you could earn money beyond trading your time for money?
sentences.zh: 心理学家们，如果你能通过出售专业知识赚钱，而不仅仅是出卖时间换金钱，会怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne Trent, clinical psychologist, and I've been developing passive and recurring income streams since 2019.
sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在开发被动和经常性收入流。

sentences.en: I have some exciting news.
sentences.zh: 我有一些令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.zh: 苏菲·富特（Sophie Foote）的一对多项目现已开放注册。

sentences.en: It's designed to help you turn your expertise into scalable offers like courses, memberships, and digital products.
sentences.zh: 它旨在帮助你将专业知识转化为可扩展的产品，如课程、会员资格和数字产品。

sentences.en: I completed the program myself in 2022 and have since supported two cohorts of psychologists through their journeys too.
sentences.zh: 我在2022年亲自完成了这个项目，此后也支持了两届心理学家学员完成他们的旅程。

sentences.en: And if you join through my affiliate link, you'll receive Sophie's bonuses plus my own exclusive support package at no extra coSt.
sentences.zh: 如果你通过我的联盟链接加入，你将获得苏菲的额外奖励以及我自己的独家支持套餐，不收取额外费用。

sentences.en: That includes six months of WhatsApp support, four group masterminds, masterclasses, personalized guidance, a Fortnum and Mason treat, and a time-limited one-to-one coaching bonus.
sentences.zh: 这包括六个月的WhatsApp支持、四个群组智囊团、大师班、个性化指导、一份福特南与梅森（Fortnum and Mason）零食礼品，以及限时一对一指导奖励。

sentences.en: Enrollment closes on Monday the 16th of November at 10 p.m.
sentences.zh: 注册将于11月16日星期一晚上10点截止。

sentences.zh: 通过说明中链接我的奖励页面了解更多信息。

sentences.zh: 请记住，你必须通过我的链接购买才能获得我的奖励。

sentences.zh: 如果你有任何问题，我随时都在这里。
